name: Azure Blob Storage (document files)

inputs.name: mapping
inputs.label: EDML mapping on this computer: a .json file, or a folder of them

inputs.name: secret
inputs.label: SAS token (read + list), connection string or account key

access: Azure: a SAS with read (r) and list (l) on this container, or the account key
auth_hint: a SAS is valid only for the container it was made for, so a wrong container name also reads as a rejected credential
tips: Tables and columns are named by the mapping file: a change to the mapping needs a new connect (exakit source remove <name>, then connect again).
A CSV mapping without fields has its columns inferred, and a date then arrives as VARCHAR(2000000): name the fields and their types in the mapping to get typed columns.
notes: The credential is one of three things Azure gives you, on standard input or through --password-file: a SAS token (recommended: limited to the container, read and list only, with an expiry), the storage account's connection string, or its account key. The kit checks a SAS on this computer first - read and list permission, not expired, not scoped to one blob - and builds the connection string itself, always over HTTPS to <account>.blob.core.windows.net.
A SAS cannot be narrowed to a folder: it opens the whole container, so keep data the database must not read in another container. An account key opens every container of the account, for writing too.
The public Azure cloud only: no custom domain, Azurite, or sovereign-cloud endpoint.

The adapter detects the file type by extension (.json, .jsonl, .csv, .parquet); CSV and Parquet can infer their columns, JSON needs explicit fields. A source glob that matches no file reads as an empty table - the check names such tables.
